page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 4.0 GB per core. A key hardware characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled local storage, consisting of 23,622 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.d1.2xlarge exhibits modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier, with scores of 1096.39 and 5838.18 respectively. Memory bandwidth read-only tests also place in the bottom 25%, although large block write performance achieves an average rating at 34.88 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show poor performance, with gzip compression scoring in the bottom 10%. Passmark CPU evaluations yield average scores for overall CPU and extended instructions, but database operations and Redis SET operations remain in the weak performance category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.d1.2xlarge offers high storage density per unit of compute, making it a viable option for workloads requiring massive local storage capacity without demanding high-performance CPU or memory throughput. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on HDD storage, which limits random I/O performance compared to SSD-based instances. This instance is best suited for sequential data processing, large-scale data archiving, log storage, and distributed file systems like HDFS where storage volume is prioritized over raw computational speed.
